name: Elaine Marquez
life: “I still remember finding dust inside a plastic daisy.” On Friday, near the brick passage off the shop row, Elaine takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.
voice: I want a cutting in the grief room because the plastic flowers look the same every morning.
appearance: Elaine has a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Look for auburn hair cut square at the nape. Out of work clothes, the familiar outfit is a gray fisher's sweater with a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial. In conversation Elaine presses the lips together to keep a smile in.
personality: Elaine finds it easier to own up to a mistake than to accept praise. The worse the mistake, the more precise the account of exactly when it happened.
agenda: To start a living plant in the grief room.
family: Aisha Ortiz is Elaine’s second cousin. Elaine offers the first invitation. Aisha gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *Level with the window*, Aisha says, “I saw my old maths teacher cooking dinner and realized he'd lived here the entire time I was away.”
connections: Lennon Adair. One inherited name and one new cutting go to rooms where the plant can be welcomed.

reactions.response: Elaine helps shift the damp stock and makes sure the worker gets to describe the loss without interruption.
